thread:
Ava: quick heads-up, we're seeing a spike in structured-output failures on canary for mix-quant-v2 (fp8+int4). ~12 failing requests in 15m, mostly missing 'items' key and some nonsense arrays. :warning:
Raj: :eyes: do we have logs/stack traces? is this the calibration change you merged yesterday?
Ava: logging attached below, repro from a canary request:
```
Request id: c2f9a5
model: mix-quant-v2
input: {'prompt': 'export inventory', 'max_tokens': 256}
response (actual): {"status":"ok","data":null}
response (expected): {"status":"ok","items":[{"sku":"X123","qty":12}],"meta":{}}
```
Also seeing structured JSON truncated to `{"items":` then newline.
Sophie: any kernel selection or batching changes in the runtime deploy last night? I remember a change to the adaptive kernel router.
Ava: yes the runtime release 2026.03.17 bumped kernel routing heuristics + introduced mixed-kernel fallback for small batches. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/842
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: mix-quant-v2 -> canary 15% (release 2026.03.17)
Noah: ran a quick perf trace on canary node 7, profiler shows a jump in KV cache lookup misses and several fallback kernel invocations for int4->fp16 on hot paths. snippet:
```
kv_cache_reads: 3782 -> 9024 (canary)
fallback_kernels_invoked: 12 -> 87
avg_token_latency(ms): 22.3 -> 31.7
l2_cache_misses: +18%
```
Noah: hypothesis: mixed-precision fallback is deoptimizing KV offsets and causing partial writes into the output buffer under specific batch alignment, leading to truncated JSON.
Raj: that matches a theoretical race in the kernel path when batch sizes change mid-request — could corrupt ring buffer offsets. Did we change batching heuristics too?
Ava: we did tweak continuous batching thresholds to be more aggressive: small-batch coalescing enabled by default.
Sophie: action: pause canary and rollback until we confirm. Can someone run the unit repro with `--random-batch-sizes` to simulate alignment issues?
Ava: repro command I'm about to run locally:
```
./tools/repro_structured_output --model mix-quant-v2 --quant-mode mixed --batch-pattern "1,3,2,5,1" --seed 1432 --iterations 500
```
Ava: also toggling kv-cache debug and kernel routing flags: `RW_RUNTIME_KERNEL_ROUTING=experimental RW_KV_DEBUG=1`
Raj: I'll prepare a short A/B test: disable adaptive routing for canary and re-run smoke evals on the failing eval set (entity-extract-tests). If error rate drops -> routing bug.
Noah: I'll instrument the kernel to assert buffer writes sizes; add an assert in small-kernel-path that verifies written bytes == expected bytes. Pushing a debug build to canary-7 now.
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: mix-quant-v2 -> previous stable (force 100%) by Ava
Ava: rollback done, canary traffic back to stable. I'll keep the failing request samples in /var/log/redwood/triage/mix-quant-v2/ for postmortem.
Sophie: quick eval deltas from canary vs stable: entity-extract F1 dropped 0.08 -> 0.55 on canary (n=200). That's significant.
Raj: tentative root cause list: 1) mixed-kernel fallback path handles KV offsets incorrectly for non-uniform batches, 2) more aggressive batching changes increased occurrence, 3) calibration rounding for int4 introduced subtle value shifts exposing downstream parser to malformed tokens.
Ava: plan: (1) keep canary rolled back, (2) run repro with `--random-batch-sizes` and debug build to capture buffer sizes, (3) add assert/logging in kernel write path, (4) run offline eval with calibration toggled to fp16 for the same model.
Noah: ETA for debug build results ~30m, will post trace and captured corrupted buffers.
Sophie: flagging on-call infra and QE to run full e2e smoke regression tomorrow morning.
Ava: thank you all — please post any short findings here. I'll open an incident doc after we confirm root cause. :white_check_mark:
